author: jsign
content:
uhm, i was checking the original [Reth optimization around this hint idea](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/stateless/blob/e3edc40a2dae527710d0ea18226384faff09a165/crates/stateless/src/recover_block.rs#L57-L78) but noticed they don't do the y-parity check I explained in the spec... so I think that was buggy.  Also see now that this code [was removed recently](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/stateless/pull/36), and they're back to full recovery.

So.. yeah, i think the current `zkvm_secp256k1_verify(..)` in the standards, we can't fully exploit this hint idea without including an extra precompile like `zkvm_secp256k1_verify_with_recovery_id(signing_hash, signature_rs, hinted_pubkey, recovery_id) -> bool` or similar.

But before proposing that prob it is worth double-checking again how much cost in mainnet blocks are for `zkvm_secp256k1_verify(..)` as is...
If we note that this is still a low % of cost, maybe this new precompile isn't worth it and we can remove `pub_keys` (woudn't oppose to that... hints in the input are a headache for the spec and testing 😅 )
